title: Expensify's Engineers on Stack Overflow for Teams
description: Expensify creates expense reports that don't suck and that ambitious work requires sophisticated technology and a talented team of engineers. Meet some of those engineers and hear how they use Stack Overflow for Teams to share knowledge with other Expensify engineers around the world and with non-engineering colleagues across the company.  Stack Overflow for Teams works for companies of all sizes, with a Business offering for mid-sized companies, and an Enterprise offering for large companies.  Learn more at stackoverflow.com/teams

asr.full_text: Expencify Expencify is expense reports that don't suck. Expencify is a cool group of people who are trying to solve the issue of completing very boring expense reports. It's a very unique company. We are essentially a flat organization. There aren't really many job titles. In practice what that means is everyday I can pick and choose the tasks that I want to work on. The way we make that work is everyone who comes to the office is trying to help everyone else. Transparency, writing things down and making sure everything we are doing everybody else can learn from. The onboarding process was... interesting we have a lot of documentation. Our documentation at Expensify has been fairly terrible in the past. People would rather talk to someone who has more knowledge than to go search through all these pages of documentation that we wrote in the past, so one of the major approaches that we took to this was implementing Stack Overflow Teams because people are already familiar with the platform. Any programmer knows how to use Stack Overflow. So to have it applied to a single code base is just that much more valuable. Stack Overflow for Teams is the beauty and the magic of Stack Overflow limited to information that is internal to the company. It's a great place to have a question and answer repository for all kinds of team and company based knowledge. People ask questions on GitHub and Slack, and those can get lost. but with Stack Overflow, they're never going to get lost in other discussions around them. We're a pretty remote company, so we utilize Slack and have a lot of international developers and developers around the country. The Slack API integration at Stack Overflow is mostly to get people to switch over their mentality of I'm going to ask this question to everybody, but it's going to get lost in Slack. Whenever there of, ìI'm gonna ask this question to everybody, but itís gonna get lost in slack.î Whenever thereís a new question, everyone gets notified. We get answers really, really quickly. One of the things we like about Expensify is that everybody can ask questions to anybody on any team, at any time, and Stack Overflow makes this very easy. Everyone has a certain amount of codebase that they are very comfortable with. But sometimes, you might know about an issue much more deeply than the so-called subject matter expert. Anybody can answer them regardless of experience. It gives an open opportunity to everyone who has the knowledge to share it, and there's no bias. I don't have to go through the hassle of like finding someone who knows the answer, figuring out if they're available or online, and then talking to them. That conversation has already happened, it's just on Stack Overflow. So it originally started as just a place for engineers because engineers were kind of used to it with the original stack overflow. But as we started to use it and see how nice it was to have a repository of information we started to see it spread to other teams. So our customer support team started using it. Our people success team started using it. Next thing we knew, we had integrations all over the place and Stack Overflow being used across the company. If I have a stupid question, probably someone else has already asked it. So when I go to Stack Overflow for Teams and I'm looking for a question, great, that saved my face. Stack Overflow for Teams saves me at least one hour every week. A couple hours saves me at least one-hour every week. Couple hours a week. Two to three hours every week. About two hours per week. Probably around two to three hours per week, but I think it's also important to note that I save other people multiple hours as well because of the answers that I'm replying to.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is a corporate testimonial about using Stack Overflow for Teams to share internal company knowledge. The offer is ordinary business software for company teams, and the claims about quick answers, team adoption, and saving work time are workplace productivity claims rather than a deceptive money-making mechanism.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central subject is an ordinary workplace technology tool and its operational use for internal questions, answers, documentation and knowledge sharing, which fits education, technology and operational demonstrations.
